correctness.rationale: Varvak's Corollary 1.3 supplies d pairwise non-isogenous Hodge-generic factors of dimension g/d, and Theorem 1.2 gives the joint group with independent symplectic factors. On H²(1) the invariants consist of the d polarization lines: in each exterior square there is one symplectic invariant and the cross terms have none. Equivalently one may take invariants of the Hodge group on H²; the weight torus of the full untwisted Mumford–Tate group must not be used as if it acted trivially there. Lefschetz (1,1) identifies this dimension with the Picard number, unchanged by isogeny. Proposition 2.8 gives the varying symmetric-power examples for every factorization g=hd, including d=1 and h=1. This proves the claim about very general smooth complex fibers of the specified primitive symplectic varieties, not about the generic fiber over the function field or the attainable counts for smooth total spaces.
residual_risks: No claim is assessed about isotrivial fibrations, special fibers or smooth attainability of intermediate divisors.

evidence: Each Hodge-generic factor has rational endomorphism algebra Q by the centralizer of its standard GSp action on H¹. Thus it is simple; pairwise non-isogenous simple factors have no cross homomorphisms. On the product, the resulting End⁰=Q^d is fixed by the Rosati involution of the product polarization, so the standard identification of NS⊗Q with Rosati-symmetric endomorphisms gives rank d.
Varvak's examples already take every d dividing g under the same primitive symplectic hypotheses; the same calculation applies unchanged to them.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Even the factor decomposition suffices by standard abelian-variety identities. The joint group gives the same rank directly. No additional geometric construction or obstruction is needed for either direction.

evidence: The rank of rational (1,1)-classes on a complex abelian variety is its Néron–Severi rank, and it is invariant under isogeny. Varvak classifies the very general complex fiber up to isogeny.
Oguiso's Theorem 1.1 treats the fiber over C(P^n); his closed-fiber example has every smooth fiber of Picard number at least two.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The Hodge invariant rank is an equivalent formulation on the complex fiber. Replacing a very general complex point by the function-field generic point is not such an equivalence and would compare the wrong theorem.

originality.rationale: Varvak supplies the full classified decomposition and realizations with the same hypotheses. The standard Picard-rank calculation on a product of pairwise non-isogenous Hodge-generic abelian varieties already implies every part of the frozen claim. The inspected source passages do not state the result in Picard-number language, but there is no new classification or example after that calculation. Oguiso concerns a different fiber, and is not used to defeat the claim.
residual_risks: The selected sources do not exhaust separately worded Picard-number corollaries. An unavailable public search is not negative evidence; the verified implication suffices for the verdict.
